eyebrow: SCRATCH AND TURBOWARP PROJECTS OPEN HERE
heading: An extensible IDE (Integrated Development Environment) for Scratch and TurboWarp projects.
intro: Open multiple panels to edit different sprites or work on the same sprite in several views at once.
introEditing: Hover to reveal controls, and drag and drop to rearrange tabs or copy blocks between sprites. Use the minimap to see how scripts are laid out. Saving a project also stores your tab and panel layout and your position in the code, so you can pick up where you left off when you reopen it.
introInspect: Inspect individual clones while your project runs and check variable and list values. Trace broadcasts in a diagram and function calls in a graph that spans sprites and the stage. Unpack your project into data and asset files and track its history with Git.
note: Opens the browser editor with a new project. To open a local SB3 or project folder, choose it from the File menu after the editor opens.
heroShot: The code area with the cat and ball sprites and their scripts
heroStageShot: The stage in its own window
heroStageCaption: Open the stage or panels in separate windows
heroSplit: Edit code side by side and see the full layout in the minimap
heroSplitShot: The minimap is visible in the lower-right corner of the right code pane
heroCalls: Trace function calls in a graph
heroCallsShot: A call graph with solid arrows from hats to functions, dashed arrows from scripts that send messages to the scripts that receive them, and gray boxes for functions in other sprites and the stage
heroDiff: In the diff view, horizontal and vertical guide bands intersect at the changed part of the script.
extensionSecurityNote: Before running a Plus-format extension, Plus Editor verifies its code against the recorded SHA-256 hash. When approval is required, review the source and execution requirements and choose whether and how to run each extension, including in a sandbox when supported.
extensionForms: Form editing for custom extension blocks
extensionFormsNote: When a compatible extension registers a JSON Schema, Plus Editor uses React JSON Schema Form to build inputs for the block’s arguments. You can edit each field, and the editor checks required values and allowed ranges before saving.
projectData: Embed structured data and DSLs in a project
projectDataNote: With a compatible extension, write settings or a domain-specific language (DSL) such as a story script in YAML or blocks, then embed it in the SB3. For example, the Kamishibai extension reads the script at runtime to switch scenes and display dialogue.
namedFunctions: Choose which function to call by name at runtime
namedFunctionsNote: With the Named Functions extension, define a function with blocks and give it a name as you write your code. At runtime, pass the name as a string, for example from a variable. The extension looks up the function by that name and runs it. Use JSON for arguments and return values, with JSON Schema to validate each.
assetDeliveryNote: In Plus Editor, choose which costume images, backdrops, and sounds to bundle with your project and which to serve over HTTPS. Reuse verified assets from the cache. Add a compatible extension such as Kamishibai to use externally hosted video.
termFeatureDef: A feature TurboWarp-Plus-Editor builds into the editor itself on top of standard TurboWarp. It works with any project. Arranging panels, project-wide search and local Git are examples.
termExtensionDef: A Scratch or TurboWarp extension that a project loads. It adds blocks and inputs or outputs such as cameras and sensors, and can also be embedded in the project and shared with it.
termAddonDef: A small feature from Scratch Addons bundled with TurboWarp. Each one can be turned on or off in the settings, and they work in TurboWarp-Plus-Editor as they are.
label: URL of the project’s SB3 file
urlNote: Use an HTTPS SB3 file that permits your browser to fetch it.
invalid: Enter a valid HTTPS URL for an SB3 project.
wayOut: A saved SB3 opens in Scratch and TurboWarp as it is
openShot: The File menu listing the ways to open a project
features: Added features: what standard TurboWarp does not have
featureOpen: Open: load progress, the Plus catalog, diagnostics when a project will not open
featureManage: Manage: read and write a project folder, local Git diffs and history, public PR review
featureArrange: Arrange: split the panels, the palette and code in separate windows, a selected function or script edited in a split tab, folding hats and definitions, the layout restored next time
featureEdit: Fix: project-wide search and replace, an edit menu, a searchable horizontal palette, a minimap, the Hats and functions and Calls sections, functions added by name, and long text arguments edited in a dialog
featureReuse: Reuse: transfer scripts and stages, add bundled assets
featureShare: Hand over: Save and Save a Copy, storage formats for data and extension code, one HTML with the Plus extensions bundled
featureCollaborate: Work with an AI: a project folder is text and ordinary files, so an agent can read and write it and you review the result as a diff or a PR
featureProperties: Project Properties: save the title, description, author, contact, and timestamps in the SB3; choose from five recent author/contact entries and open email/HTTPS links
featureDiagnostics: Project Diagnostics: inspect and copy validation, execution approval, loading, and failure records
featureProjectTools: Open Project Properties from the File menu, and Project Diagnostics from that dialog’s “Project Diagnostics…” button. Save the SB3 after applying properties; diagnostics last only while the page remains open. No supporting extension or activation option is required.
featureCondition: Forms, documents, and previews require supporting extensions.
featureGuideNote: Walks through the added features with real screenshots and diagrams, in the order you use them.
featureGuideShot: A project-wide search listing where a message is sent and received
chapterWorkspace: Split the workspace and open panels separately
chapterGit: Manage projects with project folders and Git
docsDevelopers: For developers of added features and extensions
developerGuideNote: Compares Plus with Scratch Addons and TurboWarp addons, specifies how added features are built into the editor, and explains how to build a new one.
developerGuideShot: The panel layout menu that Plus adds
featurePlatform: Extensions are not only something you use. Add one from the catalog, choose how its code is stored, embed one you wrote yourself in the SB3, and pin its name, sandbox requirement and SHA-256 with sb3-toolchain. Writing extensions in TypeScript is the recommended path: you write against typed APIs and can pull libraries straight from npm. A domain expert can also define a DSL as a JSON Schema and its documents, and let the project operate it. The extensions and apps you can use are listed on the TurboWarp Plus family page. With Plus extensions for shared camera streams, camera calibration, AR, QR reading, Teachable Machine recognition and asynchronous input, an interactive work or a camera or sensor host application is an extension plus a project, not a fork of the Editor.
family: The TurboWarp Plus family of extensions
workflowTitle: Connect block editing with your other tools
workflowIntro: Unpack a project into a project folder to work with its data, assets, and extensions as files. Edit with VS Code or an AI app, then return to the Editor to run the project and review the changes.
workflowFolderNote: Choose “Create project folder” in the left drawer to unpack the open SB3. Subsequent saves write to that same folder.
workflowFolderShot: The actual Editor showing the project folder and project.source.json
workflowFolderCaption: Inspect file content with the Normal view / Diff view capsule toggle and the minimap.
workflowDiagramAlt: Save a project folder in the Editor, edit its files with VS Code or Claude Code and Codex, then return to the Editor to load changes, test the project, review Git diffs, and commit
workflowDiagramCaption: Example workflow diagram. A shared project folder carries changes between the tools.
workflowVSCodeNote: Open the Editor through the local companion and choose “Edit in VSCode” in a file tab. Save in VSCode, choose “Finish and import edits”, then “Save file”. The tab is disabled during external editing.
workflowAINote: Give Claude Code, Codex, or another AI app that reads and writes local files access to your project folder. Ask it to change a script, for example to change the cat’s movement speed, then test the result and review the block diff in the Editor.
workflowGit: Compare and record changes with Git
workflowGitNote: Review changed files and block diffs in Local Git, then commit. Choose a past commit in Git History to trace its changes. Use branches and pull requests to review work with others.
workflowReload: Save in the Editor and stop the project before editing externally. Script changes apply automatically when there are no unsaved edits. Changes to assets or variables require a full project reload; when you have unsaved edits, compare the versions and choose what to keep.
urlAction: Open the project at this URL
projectNote: Opens the project specified in the URL in the browser editor. Save your edits from the File menu.
